intro: Two trees protected by the Azores stand in parishes just outside Angra do Heroísmo, on Terceira, rather than in its historic centre. In Posto Santo, about four kilometres north, a cork oak classified in 1985 grows in the church square, and a summary of its decree calls it the only cork oak on the island. In Terra Chã, about three kilometres west, a til, a laurel at home in Madeira and the Canaries, has been a tree of public interest since 1966. Each is about ten minutes from the centre by car.
meta_description: Two protected trees near Angra do Heroísmo, Terceira: the cork oak of Posto Santo and the til of Terra Chã, where they stand and how to reach them.
question_meta: Near Angra do Heroísmo, Terceira, two protected trees stand outside the centre, a cork oak in Posto Santo and a til in Terra Chã.
question_answer: Two protected trees near Angra do Heroísmo are worth the short trip out of the centre. The cork oak in the church square of Posto Santo, about 4 km north, was classified in 1985, and a summary of its decree calls it the only cork oak on Terceira. The til of Terra Chã, about 3 km west on Canada de Belém, has been a tree of public interest since 1966. Each is roughly ten minutes from the centre by car or taxi.
question_context: Neither tree is in Angra's historic centre, and bus connections to Posto Santo and Terra Chã have not been checked, so plan on a car or a taxi. The cork oak is classified of municipal interest under a regional decree of May 1985, confirmed in the Azores' 2015 list; by the decree's description it stands between the parish church and the parish council building, and it can be seen for free from the square. The decree's full text could not be read, so its claim that this is the island's only cork oak is reported, not checked. The til is classified of public interest, by an order of July 1966; a 2006 photograph captioned at Terra Chã gives 1965. Its pin is approximate, taken from Street View in 2020, which suggests it stands by the road; whether it grows on private ground behind a wall is not established, so look from the road. Neither tree has a published girth, height or age, and neither has a dated sighting from recent years. A photograph from either spot would settle that.

faq.q: Are these trees in Angra's historic centre?
faq.a: No. The cork oak is in the church square of Posto Santo, about 4 km north, and the til is on Canada de Belém in Terra Chã, about 3 km west. Each is about ten minutes from the centre by car or taxi.

faq.q: Is the Posto Santo cork oak the only one on Terceira?
faq.a: That is how a summary of its 1985 decree describes it. The decree's full text could not be read to confirm the wording, so treat it as the decree's claim.

faq.q: Can you visit the til of Terra Chã?
faq.a: It appears to stand by the public road on Canada de Belém, but its pin is approximate and it may grow on private ground behind a wall, so see it from the road.

trees.name: Cork Oak of Posto Santo

location.address: Largo da Igreja, Posto Santo, Angra do Heroísmo, Terceira

trees.story:
If the decree that protects it is right, this is the only cork oak on Terceira. The Azores classified it in May 1985, and a summary of that decree describes it as the one tree of its species on the island, with a size that suggests great age. The decree's own text could not be read in full, so take both as the decree's words as reported.

It stands in Largo da Igreja, the church square of Posto Santo, a parish about four kilometres north of the centre of Angra do Heroísmo. By the same description it grows between the parish church and the parish council building. The classification is of municipal interest, and the Azores confirmed it when they listed their protected trees again in 2015.

Nobody has published a girth, a height or a date for it, so its age is an open question. If you know when it was planted, or what the village says about it, tell us.

There is a second gap, and it matters more. No dated photograph or sighting from recent years has turned up, so the register and the map are the latest word on it. If you stand in that square, a photograph settles whether it is still there.

It costs nothing to see from the square. From the centre of Angra it is about ten minutes by car or taxi; a bus connection has not been checked.

trees.name: Til of Terra Chã

location.address: Canada de Belém, Terra Chã, Angra do Heroísmo, Terceira

trees.story:
The til is a laurel whose home is Madeira and the Canaries, and on Terceira this one has been a tree of public interest since July 1966. It is an evergreen of the laurel family, introduced to the Azores, and it grows in Terra Chã, a parish about three kilometres west of the centre of Angra do Heroísmo.

The register gives a road, Canada de Belém, and nothing else. No girth, no height, no age. Its position came from Street View in December 2020, which suggests the tree stands by the public road, so the pin is approximate. Whether it grows behind a wall on private ground has not been established. See it from the road.

The photograph on this page was taken in 2006 by a local Wikimedia contributor. Its caption describes a til at Terra Chã classified as a monument since 1965, a year earlier than the register's date. It is the only classified til reported in the parish, which is why it is taken to be this tree, though nothing ties the picture to the register entry directly.

That 2020 Street View image is the latest trace of it. No dated sighting since has turned up, and nobody has dated the tree itself. If you pass along Canada de Belém, tell us whether it still stands, and how old the parish thinks it is.

It is about ten minutes from the centre of Angra by car; a bus connection has not been checked.
